context: Community detection network graph (100 nodes, 5 communities) with a linked sortable table showing degree and betweenness centrality per node, using D3 force simulation.
first_impression: Structurally honest visualization with correct encoding choices throughout.
what_works: Node radius uses d3.scaleSqrt (area-correct, not radius-linear deception); betweenness bar scale uses domain [0, d3.max(data)] giving a true zero baseline; both scales are data-driven (d3.extent / d3.max), not hardcoded; node join uses a key function (d => d.id) ensuring object constancy.
what_doesnt: Sort comparison function has a dead-code branch — both the 'label' and numeric paths execute identical d3.ascending calls, so string vs. numeric sort behaves the same (minor correctness bug, not an encoding integrity issue); betweenness is approximated from only 25 BFS samples but this is undisclosed in the UI, slightly misrepresenting precision of displayed values.
